subject: Banking
title: The Credit Score Myth
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Credit Score Myth usable.

hook.text: Checking your own credit score does not lower it. This is one of the most persistent and costly myths in personal.

buildup.text: Soft inquiries like checking your own score or employer checks don't affect it.

discovery.text: A hard inquiry drops your score 5-10 points. But rate shopping for a mortgage within 14-45 days counts as only one.

twist.text: 50 million Americans have never checked their credit report.

climax.text: Not checking your score is riskier than checking it. Errors and fraud go undetected when nobody looks.

punchline.text: Checking your score won't lower it. Not checking is the real risk.

quiz.question: Does checking your own credit score lower it?
options: No, self-checks are soft inquiries that don't affect your score
